name: Adnan Khashoggi
milestone_by_age_26: Engaged by Lockheed as their Saudi agent at age 26, having already brokered a Kenworth truck-leasing deal worth approximately $250,000 and become the Saudi agent for Kenworth Trucks.
early_history_summary: Born to the personal physician of Saudi Arabia's founding king in Mecca, Khashoggi attended the elite Victoria College in Alexandria where he earned his first commission brokering a deal between classmates' families. While attending US universities, he identified opportunities linking American companies with Saudi oil wealth and began importing Kenworth trucks to the kingdom.
family_context_summary: Born to Muhammad Khashoggi, personal physician to King Abdul Aziz of Saudi Arabia, and Samiha Ahmed in Mecca. Father's court position provided direct access to the Saudi royal family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was the king's personal physician, granting the family proximity to power and royal networks; this political access was directly transferable to Khashoggi's brokering career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: royal court access, elite schooling, Saudi oil boom, royal family network
evidence_summary: Born to the personal physician of Saudi Arabia's founding king, Khashoggi grew up with direct access to the Saudi royal family. He attended Victoria College in Alexandria, an elite school where classmates included future kings of Jordan and Iraq. He made his first commission as a teenager brokering a towels deal between classmates' fathers. While at US universities, he brokered a Kenworth truck deal worth ~$250K and was engaged by Lockheed as their Saudi agent at age 26, launching his career as one of history's most famous arms dealers.
starting_point: Born in Mecca to the personal physician of Saudi Arabia's founding king; grew up with direct access to the royal family and elite education at Victoria College in Alexandria.
current_position: Died in London on June 6, 2017 at age 81; fortune had diminished significantly from his 1980s peak of ~$4 billion.

name: Petra Burka
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in ladies' figure skating at the 1964 Innsbruck Olympics at age 17, and World Championship gold in 1965 at age 18.
early_history_summary: Born in Amsterdam to Dutch figure skater and coach Ellen Burka, Petra moved to Canada in 1951 and began skating at age 10-11 under her mother's coaching. She won the Canadian junior title in 1961 at age 15 and became the first woman to land a triple Salchow in competition.
family_context_summary: Born to Ellen Burka, a Dutch figure skater and coach, and Czech-born artist Jan Burka in Amsterdam. Family immigrated to Canada in 1951; parents divorced in mid-1950s. Mother was a Holocaust survivor.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Ellen Burka was a competitive figure skater and coach who directly trained Petra from age 10-11, providing sustained expert coaching throughout her early career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother-coached, figure skating lineage, early specialization, Maple Leaf Gardens access, Holocaust survivor family
evidence_summary: Petra Burka was born to Dutch figure skater and coach Ellen Burka, who directly coached her from age 10-11 after the family immigrated to Canada. She won the Canadian junior title at 15 and became the first woman to land a triple Salchow in competition. Toronto Maple Leafs co-owner Stafford Smythe arranged for her to train at Maple Leaf Gardens before hockey players arrived, providing crucial ice time when funds were running low. She won Olympic bronze at 17 and World Championship gold at 18.
starting_point: Born in Amsterdam to Dutch figure skater and coach Ellen Burka and Czech-born artist Jan Burka; family immigrated to Canada in 1951 with limited financial means.
current_position: Former competitive figure skater working as a coach and skating consultant for Team Canada; resides in Canada.

name: Jacksepticeye
milestone_by_age_26: Reached 1 million YouTube subscribers in 2014 at age 24, making YouTube his full-time job; grew to 10 million subscribers by age 26 in 2016.
early_history_summary: Born in Ballinasloe, Ireland and raised in Cloghan, County Offaly, Seán McLoughlin played video games from age 7. He started uploading to YouTube in December 2012 while studying at Limerick Institute of Technology, and the channel grew rapidly, reaching 1 million subscribers by 2014.

evidence_summary: Seán McLoughlin grew up in rural Ireland playing video games from age 7 and started uploading YouTube videos in December 2012 at age 22 while studying music technology. By September 2013 he had only 2,500 subscribers, but the channel grew explosively, reaching 1 million by 2014 when it became his full-time job, and 10 million by 2016 at age 26. His two-videos-per-day output schedule and energetic persona drove rapid audience growth on the YouTube Let's Play wave.

current_position: One of Ireland's most popular YouTubers with ~28 million subscribers; runs clothing and coffee businesses; resides in Ireland.

name: Oksana Chusovitina
milestone_by_age_26: Won vault gold at the 1990 Goodwill Games at age 15 and Olympic team gold at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 17, both well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Bukhara, Uzbekistan (then Soviet Union), Chusovitina began gymnastics at age 7 in 1982 when her brother took her to a gymnastics class. She won the USSR Junior National all-around title at age 13 in 1988 and was competing internationally by 1990, winning vault gold at the Goodwill Games.
family_context_summary: Youngest of four children in Bukhara, Uzbekistan; her brother introduced her to gymnastics. Family was supportive but not documented as affluent or having athletic background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family background in gymnastics or sports.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet gymnastics system, early specialization, USSR Junior Nationals, vault specialist
evidence_summary: Chusovitina began gymnastics at age 7 in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, entering the elite Soviet gymnastics pipeline. She won the USSR Junior National all-around at 13, vault gold at the 1990 Goodwill Games at 15, and Olympic team gold at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at 17. Her unprecedented career longevity — competing in eight Olympic Games across three decades — is unmatched in gymnastics, but her first material milestones came well before age 26.
starting_point: Born in Bukhara, Uzbekistan (then Soviet Union) as the youngest of four children; brother introduced her to gymnastics at age 7.
current_position: Still competing as an elite gymnast at age 49; targeting the 2024 Paris Olympics; inducted into International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 2017; resides in Uzbekistan.

name: John Devitt
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in the 4x200m freestyle relay and silver in the 100m freestyle at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics at age 19.
early_history_summary: Born in Granville, New South Wales, Devitt grew up 250 metres from the Granville Olympic Pool and learned to swim through a government-funded program. He was trained by Tom Penny at the Clyde Swim Club and later Manly Swim Club, and was named captain of the Australian swimming team at the 1956 Olympics at age 19.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Granville, New South Wales, 250 metres from the Granville Olympic Pool. Educated at Catholic schools. Family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family background in swimming or sports.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian swimming system, Tom Penny coaching, Olympic pool proximity, relay team
evidence_summary: John Devitt grew up 250 metres from the Granville Olympic Pool and was trained by Tom Penny from a young age, including unconventional warm-water training at White Bay power station. He was named captain of the Australian swimming team at the 1956 Olympics at age 19, winning gold in the 4x200m relay and silver in the 100m freestyle. He later won 100m freestyle gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics. His proximity to facilities, dedicated coaching, and the dominant Australian swimming pipeline were key early advantages.
starting_point: Born in Granville, New South Wales, Australia, 250 metres from the Granville Olympic Pool; learned to swim through a government-funded Learn to Swim program.
current_position: Died on August 17, 2023 at age 86 in Sydney; final role was respected elder of Australian swimming and Olympic sports administration.

name: Mary Quant
milestone_by_age_26: Opened the boutique Bazaar on King's Road, Chelsea in November 1955 at age 25, which became an immediate commercial and cultural success and launched her career as one of the most influential fashion designers of the 20th century.
early_history_summary: Born in Woolwich, London to Welsh schoolteacher parents, Quant studied illustration at Goldsmiths College and apprenticed to a Mayfair milliner. In November 1955, with her boyfriend Alexander Plunket Greene and photographer Archie McNair, she opened Bazaar on King's Road, Chelsea, which was an immediate success.
family_context_summary: Born to Jack and Mildred Quant, Welsh schoolteachers who both earned first-class honours degrees at Cardiff University. Parents dissuaded her from fashion study; mother later lectured at London College of Fashion.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were schoolteachers with academic backgrounds; no direct fashion industry connections, though mother later taught at London College of Fashion. Parents' academic values led to compromise of attending art school instead of fashion school.
primary_early_advantage_tags: King's Road Chelsea, Swinging Sixties, Plunket Greene partnership, Bazaar boutique, youth fashion movement
evidence_summary: Mary Quant was born to Welsh schoolteacher parents in London and studied illustration at Goldsmiths College, where she met her future husband and business partner Alexander Plunket Greene. After apprenticing to a Mayfair milliner, she opened Bazaar on King's Road, Chelsea in November 1955 at age 25 with Plunket Greene and Archie McNair. The boutique was an immediate success, selling out within ten days. Located at the epicenter of what became Swinging London, Quant's self-taught designs revolutionized youth fashion and she became one of the most influential designers of the 20th century, compared to Chanel and Dior.
starting_point: Born in Woolwich, London to Welsh schoolteacher parents who both earned first-class honours degrees at Cardiff University; middle-class upbringing with academic expectations.
current_position: Died on April 13, 2023 at age 93 in Surrey, England; final status was Dame and one of the most influential fashion designers of the 20th century.

name: Takeshi Kitano
